story.title: Fairphone’s next repairable wireless earbuds will launch on October 14th

facts.text: Following leaks revealing a major redesign earlier this month and an official teaser posted to X yesterday, Fairphone has shared some exclusive details with The Verge about the first follow-up to its Fairbuds wireless earbuds that debuted over two years ago.
Fairphone says the Fairbuds 2 will launch in Europe first for €119, followed by a US release where they’ll be available for $119.
Fairphone will unveil the Fairbuds 2 wireless earbuds on October 14, retaining the repairable modular design of the previous model.
As The Verge reports , the new product will have seven fully replaceable modular parts.
The original Fairbuds were among the first wireless earbuds designed with replaceable components.
The company has already published a teaser for the upcoming model, while media outlets had previously reported leaks about its substantially updated design.
In Europe, Fairbuds 2 will be sold for €119, and the model will later be released in the United States at a price of $119.
At the start of sales in 2024, Fairbuds cost €149, or approximately $162 at the time.
The new earbuds will also support Sony’s high-quality adaptive LDAC Bluetooth codec.
The first version of Fairbuds worked only with SBC and AAC codecs.
